artists.biography: Belly was an alternative rock band formed in 1991 by former Throwing Muses members Tanya Donelly (who was also in The Breeders) and Fred Abong. The band was based in Boston, Massachusetts, though all of the original members grew up in Newport, Rhode Island. The band consisted of Donelly on lead vocals and guitar, Abong on bass, Tom Gorman on guitar, and Chris Gorman on drums. Tom and Chris, who were brothers, were childhood friends of Donelly's; they had previously played in the hardcore punk band Verbal Assault. On at least one tour date (in February, 1993) in Albany, NY, former Throwing Muses member, Leslie Langston, lent a hand on bass.

perplexity.description:
Bees" is a compilation album by the American alternative rock band Belly, originally released in 2021. The album gathers a collection of B-sides and cover songs recorded during the band's career, offering fans a deeper look into their creative output beyond their main studio albums. Musically, "Bees" showcases Belly's signature blend of dreamy melodies, jangly guitar textures, and Tanya Donelly's distinctive vocals, reflecting the band's roots in the 1990s alternative rock scene while highlighting their versatility across different styles and moods.

In the context of Belly's discography, "Bees" serves as a companion piece to their three studio albums, arriving after their 2018 comeback record "Dove." Released to coincide with the band's 30th anniversary and as a Record Store Day exclusive, the compilation underscores Belly's enduring connection to the 4AD label and their legacy in the indie rock world. While not a commercial blockbuster, "Bees" was well-received by fans and critics for its nostalgic value and the quality of its rarities, reaffirming Belly's influence and the lasting appeal of their sound.
